intent: The button whose press opens its Popover, and optionally its hover.
typical_uses: The control that opens a panel of settings or filters beside it

dont_use_when.situation: A button that opens a list of actions
A text hint shown on hover or focus
A link whose preview shows on hover

invariants.text: PopoverTrigger renders a native button with no kit class of its own; its look comes from `className` or from the element passed through `render`.

The trigger carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and an `aria-expanded` that is true while the popover is open and was opened by this trigger; while the popover is open, the trigger that opened it, or the only trigger when none is recorded as the opener, also carries `aria-controls` with the popup's id.

A press toggles the popover; hover opens it only with `openOnHover`, for mouse pointers, once the pointer has rested on the trigger for `delay` milliseconds (300 when not given), and a popover opened by hover closes `closeDelay` milliseconds (0 when not given) after the pointer leaves both the trigger and the popup.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a non-button element through `render` while `nativeButton` stays at its default
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `nativeButton={false}` together with a `render` element that is not a native button, so the primitive adds the button role and keyboard handling itself

a11y.by: the primitive's Popover.Trigger renders a native button with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded; popover.test.tsx asserts getByRole('button', { name: 'Open' }) on it and that clicking it opens the popup ("opens on trigger click and renders content with kit classes")

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's Popover.createHandle(), tying this trigger to a Popover root it is not placed inside
handle.because: `PopoverHandle<Payload>` is a class instance holding the popover's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

payload.states: payload is any value handed to the root's function children when this trigger opens the popover
payload.because: Typed by the caller's own `Payload` type parameter (`unknown` here), so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, open). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit sets no style of its own on the trigger.

good.title: The kit's Button rendered as the trigger
An icon button that also opens on hover, with an action in its panel
good.code:
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger openOnHover delay={150} aria-label="About quotas">
    <InfoIcon />
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>
    <PopoverTitle>Quota</PopoverTitle>
    <Button variant="outline" onClick={requestMore}>Request more</Button>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>

bad.title: A kit Button nested inside the trigger
bad.why: The trigger already renders a native button, so this nests a button inside a button, which HTML does not allow; pass the Button through `render` instead.
